[UX] Why there still exists a (anchor) tag with javascript:void() or # as href for navigation?

The <a href="javascript:void()">Text</a> tag. I can't post it in the title for security reason. And I can't edit the post message either.

I hate them. I cannot open it in new tab and what's worse, they can't be indexed. Why prefer javascript:void() over href link with onlick override?

Typically you'll find a chunk of javascript somewhere that sets up an explicit click handler on that link. Putting that "javascript:void(0)" bit as the href is a way to make it so that the link itself won't actually redirect you anywhere when clicked. Instead, the custom click handler gets fired and no redirection occurs (from the click itself- the handler function would be totally able to redirect you away if that's what it needs to do though).

edit I just reread your post- thought you were wondering what that bit did in general. Yeah, I much prefer just having a standard onclick handler that just returns false/true on whether it should redirect. Always annoying popping open a blank tab.
